column1: # factors-mux.tsv — the twelve knobs the first mux screen moves.
#   go run ./bench/screen gen -factors bench/screen/factors-mux.tsv -runs 16 > variants.txt
# Format: <knob> <low> <high>, whitespace separated; # lines are prose.
# TWELVE FACTORS NEED A 16-RUN DESIGN. A 12-run Plackett-Burman holds at most
# eleven; drop a line to use -runs 12, or spend -runs 24 to buy a second estimate
# of every effect. At 3 trials and a 50 MB cell, 16 runs is 16 design rows plus
# the 16 interleaved baseline rows per trial.
# EVERY FACTOR HERE IS LIVE MID-SESSION. bench/run-variants.sh dials one session
# and then only writes knobs between rows, so a knob read at DIAL time or when a
# route group is BUILT would be measured as if it had done nothing. Those are
# named at the bottom, deliberately out.
# The low/high pairs bracket the compiled default in each direction, which is
# what makes a main effect a statement about the direction to move a knob rather
# than about one arbitrary value.
# leg.starve_ratio (default 6.0) — the outclassed-leg gate: how far off the best
# leg's delay basis a leg may sit before it is cut to a probe per window. The
# storm fix of 2026-09-16 and the 2-leg retx storms both live here, and nothing
# has ever measured whether 6.0 is the right place to cut.
leg.starve_ratio
# ecf.max_window_bytes (default 8MiB) — the per-leg send window ceiling. The
# open 2-leg question from the campaign: a ceiling too low starves aggregation,
# too high buys in-flight bytes that only turn into reorder work.
ecf.max_window_bytes
# ecf.window_margin (default 2.0) — the multiplier on proven delivery-per-RTT
# that sets the window in the first place. It and the ceiling above are the two
# halves of one control and the screen can tell which half is binding.
ecf.window_margin
# band.demote_ratio_tight (default 2.0) — how far off the median latency an
# active leg may sit in CAPACITY mode before it is demoted. This is the knob
# that decides whether a slow-but-real route is spread across or thrown away,
# which is the bittorrent-like-spread objective stated in prose.
band.demote_ratio_tight
# rack.reorder_factor (default 1.25) — the reordering tolerance before a
# sequence is presumed lost. Multipath reorders by construction; too tight is a
# retransmit storm, too loose is head-of-line delay.
rack.reorder_factor
# reorder.window (default 32768) — how many out-of-order packets the receiver
# holds. The no-skip frontier means this is also how deep a stall may get before
# the last-resort drop, and 32768 has never been measured against anything.
reorder.window
# tlp.pto_factor (default 2.0) — the tail-loss probe timeout as a multiple of
# the slowest leg's RTT. It governs the end of every chunk, and a 4 MiB chunked
# download is almost all tails.
tlp.pto_factor
# hol.rtt_factor (default 1.0) — the gap age, in fastest-leg RTTs, at which a
# proactive head-of-line retransmit fires. The HoL wall is the documented reason
# multipath aggregation fails; this is the knob that attacks it directly.
hol.rtt_factor
# sbd.enabled (default true) — shared-bottleneck detection at all. It is on and
# sbd.demote is off, so it currently only records rulings: the screen says
# whether the sampling itself costs anything measurable.
sbd.enabled
# chunk.tunnel_concurrency (default 4) — chunks one tunnel may carry at once on
# a split download. The download composition cap (~6.5 MB/s at 100 MB) is a
# placement question before it is a scheduler question.
chunk.tunnel_concurrency
# chunk.per_tunnel (default 2) — how many chunks the planner aims to give each
# active tunnel, which sets how wide a transfer is spread before the scheduler
# ever sees it.
chunk.per_tunnel
# upload.concurrency (default 4) — chunks one tunnel may carry at once on a
# striped upload. The 10 MB upload gap (x0.5-0.65) is the longest-standing
# unexplained cell in the campaign and this is its first suspect.
upload.concurrency
# DELIBERATELY OUT, and why:
#   fec.enabled, mux.sack, mux.per_frame_noise, mux.hol_retx — advertised on NEW
#     route groups only; a session already up keeps what it was born with.
#   dial.candidates, dial.tunnel_legs, dial.foreground_mux, setup.* — read while
#     a dial is CHOOSING a route. Screening them needs a re-dial per run, which
#     is 30-70 s of settling per row and a different runner.
#   pool.size, tunnel.count, mux.width — they change the SHAPE (how many tunnels
#     carry the transfer), so a run that moves them is not comparable to one that
#     does not; shape belongs in run-mux.sh / run-standby.sh sets.
#   spread.max_share, spread.min_routes — criterion 10's policy, scored by
#     bench/direction.sh against a cap assert, not by throughput alone.
#   tunnel.promote_goodput_margin, tunnel.audition_every — the promoter acts over
#     minutes; a 50 MB row is too short to move it, so it needs run-standby.sh.
